content_voiceover: This diagram summarizes anaplastic large cell lymphoma, ALCL, which is defined immunophenotypically by strong, uniform CD30 expression, shown here on the immunohistochemistry image. ALCL splits based on ALK status. ALK positive ALCL is always systemic, and one hundred percent of cases harbor an ALK gene rearrangement, most commonly the NPM-ALK fusion from t two;five, which drives constitutive activation of STAT3 as the key downstream effector. ALK negative ALCL is driven instead by JAK-STAT pathway mutations rather than ALK rearrangement, and it can present as either a systemic form or, importantly, a primary cutaneous form, cALCL, which behaves very differently and is generally indolent. For prognosis, the ranking to memorize is that ALK positive systemic ALCL outperforms ALK negative systemic ALCL, and ALCL as a category outperforms CD30 positive PTCL more broadly. So the exam-relevant hierarchy is: ALK positive beats ALK negative, and having the CD30 positive ALCL phenotype is a favorable prognostic marker within the T-cell lymphoma spectrum, largely because it makes patients eligible for brentuximab vedotin, the anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate.
keypoints: ALCL = CD30-positive large cell lymphoma; splits into ALK+ vs ALK- subtypes
ALK+ ALCL: 100% ALK rearrangement (often NPM-ALK), STAT3 key effector, always systemic
ALK- ALCL: JAK-STAT mutations; can be systemic or primary cutaneous (cALCL)
Prognosis ranking: ALK+ ALCL > ALK- ALCL > CD30+ PTCL
CD30 positivity predicts brentuximab vedotin eligibility
keypoint_voiceover: Remember the prognosis ladder: ALK positive ALCL beats ALK negative ALCL, and ALCL as a whole beats CD30 positive PTCL more broadly. ALK positive disease is always systemic, driven by ALK rearrangement activating STAT3. ALK negative disease is driven by JAK-STAT mutations instead, and can be systemic or purely cutaneous. Because ALCL is uniformly CD30 positive, these patients are candidates for brentuximab vedotin.
